//: Machine-local overrides for the deliver/pr-* skill family. Copy to ~/.agents/local/config.json and fill in. Never commit the filled-in copy: it names private repos, hosts and bot accounts.
//protected_branches_extra: Branch patterns that are ALSO protected, on top of the built-in main, master and stage-*. Entries are glob patterns: a bare name matches exactly, * matches any run of characters, so "rc-*" covers every dated release candidate. Used by deliver, pr-open, pr-babysit, pr-merge.
//pr_review_default_repo: owner/repo that pr-review targets when the cwd has no useful origin remote. Omit to always derive from git remote get-url origin.
//rebase_sync_repos: owner/repo entries whose CLAUDE.md mandates rebase-before-push. For these, pr-babysit/pr-merge rebase onto the target and force-push with --force-with-lease instead of merging forward.
//ai_reviewer_usernames_gitlab: GitLab usernames of AI reviewers, added to the built-in list. Comments from these are auto-addressed; everything else batches as human.
//ai_reviewer_usernames_github: GitHub usernames of AI reviewers, added to the built-in ["cursor"]. The [bot] suffix is stripped before matching.
//sonar_host_url: SonarQube base URL. Omit or leave empty to skip the SonarQube phase entirely.
//bot_noise_body_markers_extra: Extra HTML-comment markers that identify a bot comment as noise, added to the built-in list.
//personal_backlog: Where post-merge-cleanup writes a deferred item that doesn't warrant a tracker ticket. Not per-repo — it's your backlog, wherever you keep it. Configure the app/destination its connector needs; that destination is then the source of truth, so nothing is also written locally to drift from it. Unset, or its connector missing this session, falls back to a local markdown note.

personal_backlog.page_url: <url of the page or database new entries go in>
personal_backlog.page_id: <its id, if the connector needs one>
personal_backlog.fallback: <what to do when the connector is unavailable>
personal_backlog.layout: <where a new entry goes, and how a finished one is marked done. E.g. a row in a Backlog database with Status = Open, Priority, Area and Source (the PR, thread or ticket it came from), set to Status = Done with a Completed date when finished, or Dropped when decided against; one page per entry, moved under a Done page when finished, works too>

//ux_guidance: Per repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>': design and copy guidance kept outside the repo, to check a UI change against (a design doc, a style guide page, a copy guide). Each source names where it lives, what it covers (design, copy, components) and, optionally, the paths it applies to. Guidance the repo itself points reviewers at, from a REVIEW.md or CLAUDE.md or as one of its own skills, needs no entry.
//voice_inbox: Where a copy of the voice skill that can't write to the repos (one uploaded to a chat app) saves a correction, for a session that can write to fold into the corpus. Holds the app, the destination, and how an entry is written and marked folded in. Unset, such a copy hands the correction back as a block to paste into a coding session instead.

voice_inbox.url: <url of the page or database entries go in>
voice_inbox.layout: <how a new entry is written and how a folded one is marked. E.g. a row in a database with Name, Genre (Slack, PR comment, PR description) and Status = New, holding the anonymized entry in its body; set to Folded in once it's in the corpus, or Skipped with a reason>

//chat_skill_uploads: Skills uploaded by hand to a chat app that can't read local files, keyed by surface (e.g. 'claude.ai'). uploader: the skill that packages a copy and uploads it there. Per skill: upload_name, what the copy is called there, which differs from the skill's own name where the app syncs its skills back into the coding agent, so the stale copy isn't mistaken for the current one; description, a short one within the app's limit that opens with when to use it ("Use for any …"), since it's all the app reads to decide whether a request needs the skill; refresh_after_days, how stale an uploaded copy may get before it's flagged. When each copy was last uploaded is state, not config: ~/.agents/local/state/chat-uploads.json.

<surface>.uploader: <skill that packages and uploads a copy>

<skill>.description: <when to use it, then what it does, within the app's limit>

//auto_approval: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>'. A repo where applying a label requests an automated review. pr-open adds it after opening when the diff meets opt_in_criterion. label: the label to add. mechanism: how it is triggered, for the report. opt_in / opt_in_criterion: when it applies and the test a diff must meet. notes: traps worth remembering. Applying it only requests a review — the bot triages risk itself and declines what it does not like — so it needs no approval gate. Omit a repo and pr-open never labels it.
//review_request_mechanism: How pr-open Step 7 asks for review. 'github-reviewers' proposes reviewers on the PR itself and skips Slack, since pinging as well splits the thread. Unset means a Slack draft via voice.
//review_request_channel: Slack channel the Step 7 draft is addressed to, when Slack is the mechanism.
//review_request_handle: Group handle to open that draft with. Preferred over naming individuals — it reaches whoever is free, which is how a claim-by-reaction channel works. Unset falls back to whoever the user names, else an @<reviewer> placeholder.
//code_review_effort: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>' with a '*' fallback, like second_opinion_review. The effort level self-review and pr-review pass to Claude Code's bundled /code-review for their correctness pass: low (only its most confident findings), medium, high, xhigh, or max (the widest, and the costliest: it starts many reviewer subagents). Unset → high. Never ultra: that is a paid cloud review, run only when the user asks for one.
//risk_reviewers: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>'. The automated reviewers that each rate a PR's risk or approve it, so pr-merge can tell when they disagree (its condition 10) and ask the user instead of merging. Each entry: name, and verdict (where its rating and its approval are read for the head commit: an approving review by its login, a label it sets, a check's summary). With fewer than two for a repo the condition doesn't apply.

github/acme/web.name: Review bot A
github/acme/web.verdict: Its review on the head: APPROVED or not, and the 'Risk: LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH' line in its body.

github/acme/web.name: Review bot B
github/acme/web.verdict: The 'Approvals' check on the head: success means it approved; the risk classifier's result in its summary is its rating.

//second_opinion_review: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>'. Turns on a second correctness pass by a different model (self-review/passes/second-opinion.md), which self-review runs on your own diff and pr-review on someone else's PR. Omit a repo and the step never runs there, unless the map has a '*' entry: the machine-wide fallback, used by any repo without an entry of its own. Set a repo's entry to false to keep it off. It is opt-in because the reviewer is handed your diff, and where that goes is a per-codebase decision, so add '*' only on a machine where every repo you'd clone may go to that vendor (a work laptop under an enterprise agreement, say). command: a non-interactive CLI taking instructions as an argument and reading content on stdin. It is run from a scratch directory, not the repo, so include whatever flag that CLI needs to accept a non-repo working directory (codex needs --skip-git-repo-check). Pin the model and reasoning effort in it too (codex: -m <model> -c model_reasoning_effort=<level>): left bare it runs whatever the CLI defaults to, which for codex was its frontier model at no reasoning at all. Pin the newest generation of a model rather than a previous one. max_rounds: how many times the convergence loop may re-run it after fixes (2 is usually enough; the cap exists because a second model will always find something on a large diff). notes: traps worth remembering.
//staging_verification: Per-repo, keyed by 'github/<owner>/<repo>'. Enables deliver's B5 staging-verification phase for repos that gate deploys on manual testing. Omit a repo and the phase never runs for it. needs_testing_label: the PR label that marks a change as needing post-deploy testing. staging_url: the deployed environment to drive. deploy_state_cmd: a command that reports whether a given sha has landed on each surface. notes: free-text traps worth remembering, appended as they cost time.

github/acme-org/example-repo.deploy_state_cmd: <command taking a sha, reporting deployed/not per surface>

//local_e2e: Per-repo, keyed the same way. Read by the exercise pass (self-review/passes/exercise.md) before driving the app locally, from self-review or pr-review. start: how to bring the stack up. app_url: where it lands. login: how to authenticate a test user. notes: traps that have cost time before — append rather than rediscover.

github/acme-org/example-repo.start: <command that brings the local stack up>

//project_context: Maps a tracker project to the one page holding its engineering background. Keyed by '<tracker>:<project id>': a Linear project, a Jira epic, whatever the tracker groups tickets by; ids rather than names, which change. The value is the page's URL, wherever it lives (Notion, Linear, Drive, a Slack canvas), or null for a project known to have none, so it isn't asked about again.
//verification_addenda: Extra verification commands for repos whose nested apps own a separate pipeline. Run by self-review and pr-merge when a changed path starts with when_paths_under.

verification_addenda.run: cd apps/example && pnpm install && pnpm lint && pnpm test && pnpm build
